sections.heading: C Variable Names
sections.body: All C variables must be identified with unique names. These unique names are called identifiers. Identifiers can be short names (like x and y) or more descriptive names (age, sum, totalVolume). Note: It is recommended to use descriptive names in order to create understandable and maintainable code:

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: The general rules for naming variables are: Names can contain letters, digits and underscores; Names must begin with a letter or an underscore (_); Names are case-sensitive (myVar and myvar are different variables); Names cannot contain whitespaces or special characters like !, #, %, etc.; Reserved words (such as int) cannot be used as names Here are some examples to help you remember the rules: Valid: age, _count, totalSum; Invalid: 1age (starts with a number), my-age (contains -), int (reserved word) Naming style: Many C programmers use camelCase (like totalScore) or underscores (like total_score). Choose one style and use it consistently.
